st: Abundance is here, just put on your sunglasses

sec.p: Futuro Fortissimo's first issue on climate and renewables went out on a cold March day four years ago ( 🎼 ff.12 Sun, heart and love ). Cold March, mind you, in Bergamo. In the south-western United States this year, a heatwave pushed temperatures to mid-June levels. In short, a…

… a quick energy guide, to put numbers and labels on things (after all, 🎼 ff.32 Numbers don't lie ). Un'ora sola ti vorrei — just one hour, as the old Italian song goes. First, a reminder of the units for power (W, often GW) and for energy produced/consumed (often TWh). How…

With these “rulers” in hand, let's measure the latest developments. In Texas - forever the symbol of American oil - 2025 saw solar output rise by 40%, peaking at 7 TWh in August (~1 GW of energy produced, i.e. our famous 450,000 Italian households). Yes, the sun doesn't shine…

Why the acceleration? By now, generating renewable electricity simply makes technological sense. One bottleneck is installation. But here another trend dear to futuro fortissimo comes to the rescue: robotics. Maximo (developed by AES, a company backed by NVIDIA) has just…
